editorial:
Imagine getting a credit card in the mail and thinking you just won the lottery, only to find out you are actually digging a massive financial hole. That is exactly where you find Frank Hopper, a former lawyer who is more of a dreamer than a winner. He decides to use this borrowed money to start an all-woman hockey team, which sounds like a great idea until you realize he has no real plan and is deeply in debt. The vibe is very lighthearted and silly, focusing on a guy who is probably not the brightest bulb in the box but has a heart of gold and a wild imagination.

You will likely enjoy how the movie balances the sports action with the courtroom drama that happens when the money runs out. The acting is solid and keeps the mood upbeat, even when Frank is in hot water. While the plot is pretty predictable, it is a great choice for a lazy Sunday afternoon.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head in the courtroom where Frank has to face the music for his spending spree. Instead of ending in total disaster, the movie wraps up with a feel-good twist. The women on the hockey team rally around Frank because he actually believed in them. He manages to find a way to settle his debts and keep the team together, proving that his crazy dream actually had some value after all.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves underdog sports stories and silly humor.
